hook: Rain falling on a farm in Minnesota, a parking lot in Pittsburgh and a ranch in Montana can all end up in the Gulf of Mexico. They share one watershed, the Mississippi's, which drains about 40% of the lower 48 states. Whatever lands on that land, from soil to fertilizer to oil from roads, can travel downstream to everyone below.

prereq.q: What is the difference between runoff and infiltration?
options: Runoff flows over the surface; infiltration soaks into the ground
Runoff soaks into the ground; infiltration flows over the surface
Both mean water evaporating from the ground
Both mean water taken up by plant roots
prereq.why: Runoff moves over the land toward streams; infiltration moves water down into soil.

options: Underground rock or sediment that stores groundwater
A river and the streams that feed it
A lake made by a dam
prereq.why: An aquifer is an underground layer whose pores hold water.

prereq.q: Why does a bare, plowed field erode faster than a grassy one?
options: No roots hold the soil and nothing shields it
Bare soil has more organic matter
prereq.why: Roots bind soil and plant cover shields it from rain and wind.

chain.cause: Rain falls anywhere inside a watershed's divide
chain.effect: it runs downhill toward the same stream, river or lake, or soaks in

chain.cause: Steep slopes, bare soil and pavement let less water soak in
chain.effect: more water runs off, faster, carrying soil and pollutants with it

chain.cause: Runoff collects in tributaries that join the main river
chain.effect: what enters anywhere upstream can reach every community downstream

chain.cause: Forests, wetlands and plant cover slow water and let it soak in
chain.effect: floods are smaller, streams are cleaner and aquifers are recharged

ideas: A watershed (drainage basin) is all the land that drains into one body of water. High ground called a divide separates one watershed from the next.
Small watersheds nest inside larger ones: a creek's watershed is part of a river's, which is part of a larger basin.
Its area, slope, soil, vegetation and land use shape how much rain runs off, how fast, and how much soil and pollution the water carries.
A watershed is land that drains to surface water; an aquifer is water stored underground in rock and sediment. Water soaking in across a watershed can recharge an aquifer.
Protecting a stream means protecting its whole watershed, because water from all of it ends up there.

misconception.wrong: A watershed is the body of water, such as a lake or an underground aquifer, that collects water.
misconception.right: A watershed is the land that drains into a body of water. An aquifer is something else: groundwater stored underground. The exam often tests this difference.

summary: A watershed is all the land that drains into one stream, river or lake, bounded by high ground called a divide. Its slope, soil, plant cover and land use control how much rain runs off and how much soil and pollution reach the water. A watershed is surface land; an aquifer is water stored underground. Whatever happens anywhere in a watershed flows downstream.
